newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil gets support from Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil gets support from Indonesia.

text.p: Singapore diesel prices were pressured by weaker gas oil futures on the IPE Tuesday, but was supported by Indonesia's huge purchases for November delivery, traders said.

Swaps gas oil for November slipped 15 cents from Monday to $30.45/$30.60 a barrel as November IPE slipped by $2.75 a tonne and crude futures also fell. A Singapore trader who sold two cargoes Monday at $30.50 and $30.40 for mid-November lifting sold another 150,000-barrel cargo Tuesday at $30.40 for Nov 13-17 fob to a Thai trader. The same trader offered another cargo at $30.20 for Nov 15-19.

Indonesia's purchase of four million barrels for November delivery, almost doubling its normal monthly imports, provided support for the gas oil market. Traders said Indonesia could still require more. Jet fuel was offered by a German trader at $30.80 for mid-November lifting with a bid at $30.10. Traders said another German trader recently sold a jet fuel cargo to Indonesia for November delivery but the price was unclear. A Japanese refiner Monday bought a jet fuel cargo for end-November delivery at $1.50 a barrel over Singapore spot quotes c+f, from a S.Korean refiner. Another Japanese refiner Friday bought from a MidEast trader at $1.35 premium for end-November arrival c+f.

Gasoline was again actively discussed for the 95-octane grade. Traders said activity had initially focussed on lower octane grades with more demand for the grade while Chinese sellers are heard offering low octane cargoes lifting in December. But on Tuesday, three buyers sought 50,000 barrel-cargoes of 95-octane unleaded lifting from Singapore in the second half of November. Bids were raised from $24.45 per barrel fob Singapore with a deal reported at $24.90 for November 23-27 by the day's end. One trader seeking 97-octane dropped his bid from Monday's $26.10 to trade at $25.85 for November 24-28. -- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3084)
